title: Launch the website
summary: Domain checked and bought, site generated, DNS wired, analytics on.

parts.title: Check domain availability
parts.guidance: Develop a short domain shortlist from the chosen brand and intended website use. Check registration availability and naming conflicts through the domain workflow, recording the exact spelling and extension. Treat availability as a point-in-time result and separate it from trademark clearance, then pass the selected candidate and purchase constraints to the authorized buyer.

parts.title: Buy a domain
parts.guidance: Purchase the approved domain using the intended company-controlled registrar account and verified registrant details. Review the checkout terms, renewal handling and access recovery before committing funds. Retain the registration confirmation and ownership controls, ensuring the website team can manage DNS without relying on a personal account or a search result that merely showed availability.

parts.title: Generate a website
parts.guidance: Build the site around the agreed audience, message, required pages and primary user action. Supply the website workflow with approved copy, brand assets and functional requirements, then review the rendered pages and key interactions. Keep the publishable version and remaining issues clear before connecting the production domain and inviting real users.

parts.title: Set up custom domain
parts.guidance: Connect the purchased domain to the site's actual hosting project using the host's current DNS instructions. Preserve records used by email and other services. Check the intended apex and www addresses, redirects and HTTPS from outside the hosting console; the handoff is a working public site at the chosen address, with any unresolved hostname issue explicit.

parts.title: Set up product analytics
parts.guidance: Instrument the deployed site's meaningful user actions and acquisition paths, using the approved measurement plan and privacy choices. Test events on the real domain and filter known test traffic appropriately. Preserve event definitions and verification evidence so the site owner can evaluate launch performance without treating an installed tracking snippet as complete analytics setup.
